newsitem.title: GERMANY: German government confirms Postbank deal.
newsitem.headline: German government confirms Postbank deal.

text.p: The German government on Friday confirmed it has agreed to allow the state-owned Post Office to take a stake of up to 17.5 percent in the banking arm of the formal postal authority Deutsche Postbank AG.

Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch said in a statement that a deal was struck between Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition parties on Thursday to limit Post Office control of Postbank and set the terms of their cooperation.
"The government expects the companies to support this agreement and see that it is carried out," the government said in a statement.
"On the basis of this agreement the federal government can ensure the privatisation of Deutsche Postbank AG this year."
The statement was released by Boetsch and Rainer Funke, Free Democrat (FDP) state secretary in the Justice Ministry, who led the coalition talks on the Post Office agreement.
The deal ends months of wrangling between Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) and his coalition partner FDP and appears to be a victory for the liberals who opposed Post Office control of the Postbank.

Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch and Finance Minister Theo Waigel had proposed that the Post Office be allowed to take up to 25 percent of Postbank, but the new deal means Post Office will not have control.
Post Office and Postbank were split off from the post ministry and set up as joint stock corporations in 1995 wholly owned by the German government but slated for privatisation.
Postbank, while separate from the Post Office, does not have its own network of branch offices, but uses counter space in post offices.

The terms of continuing this relationship between the Postbank and Post Office has been at the centre of their dispute and one of the reasons why Post Office had sought management control of Postbank.
According to the agreement reached late on Thursday, Post Office would be allowed to take a stake of up to 17.5 percent in Postbank via a capital increase.

The deal also states that Postbank will pay Post Office up to 37.5 million marks ($22.1 million) each year for use of Post Office counters to distribute its banking services. A cooperation agreement will be ready for signing by the parties on March 17.
Postbank has also agreed to put off any decision regarding other strategic partners until a basic agreement with the Post Office and the federal government is reached regarding such alliances.
Both the Post Office and Postbank will be represented by one member on each company's supervisory board.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.694 German Marks)
